objective: Give a uniform same-order split domination certificate for the missing-own-group chordal family with unbounded neighborhood-class count, exact residual reuse, and a separately scoped crossing-edit repair.

atomic_claims.text: Midpoint coloring for odd b, or one dummy label for even b, gives explicit q^2 triangle allocations with every remaining crossing and core link identified.
For every b>=2 and q>=1 the specified chordal clique-group family G_(b,q) satisfies cp<=B(2bq) and cp<=n^2/8+n; the constants do not depend on b.
For odd b, disjoint core-label pairs with distinct midpoint colors permit explicit K_(3q) coalescence and the bound (b-1)^2*q^2/2+b+1.
The small-mixed-piece alternative with arbitrary outside F and D deletions/A additions has cp<=P_b(q)+p_F+D+A, yielding an exact sufficient benchmark criterion.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs and exact edge-disjoint clique partitions.
The specified equal-size missing-own-group pattern; b and q are otherwise arbitrary.
The unedited nonsplit conclusion assumes each outside group is a clique and different outside groups are nonadjacent.
Edited inputs require a separate chordality check before applying the domination conclusion.
C01 matching construction and C15/C16 explicit resource-accounting inputs.
risks: Natural-language proof draft only; no mathematical execution or verifier receipt.
The unbounded-class conclusion does not remove the equal-size or specific neighborhood-pattern restrictions.
The large-piece improvements do not inherit the D+A repair cost; the small-piece alternative is used for repairs.
The benchmark is attained by a split graph, not asserted as the maximum for all split graphs.
The earlier fixed b=4 construction can be sharper; alternative savings are not added.
